Article Title: 'Resignations are part of politics': DKS on two Congress MLAs quitting over Karnataka cabinet snub
Article Text:
I too was denied a ministerial berth, but didn't resign, said DK Shivakumar after 2 Congress MLAs quit.

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday downplayed the resignation of two Congress MLAs who quit the legislative assembly after being left out of the state cabinet expansion, saying "it is a part of politics. "Shivakumar said, "Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay."Drawing from his own political journey, the chief minister said he too had been denied ministerial berths in the past but chose to remain with the party."If there is a party, everything else follows. When I was denied a ministerial berth during the tenures of Dharam Singh and Siddaramaiah, I could have resigned too. Didn't G Parameshwara and I remain patient?" he said.Shivakumar also said he had directed all ministers to immediately visit their respective districts to assess the drought relief situation.The remarks came a day after Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, expressing disappointment over being excluded from the cabinet expansion.Patil submitted his resignation to Deputy Speaker Rudrappa Lamani at the Vidhana Soudha. Soon after, his supporters staged a protest in Bengaluru, alleging that he had been treated unfairly by the party.Gopalakrishna also resigned, adding to the pressure on the Congress leadership ahead of the swearing-in ceremony for the new ministers.Speaking to reporters, Patil claimed his name had been included in the list of ministers until the last moment but was dropped from the final announcement."I have been watching the developments within the party; ultimately today, during the expansion, our leadership failed to keep the promise made. So, without any other option, it was inevitable for me to resign. I have submitted the resignation," he said."It is not acceptable to my conscience. The situation in Vijayapura district is that loyalty and honesty are not valued in the Congress party . I have no other choice. I will speak to my supporters and well-wishers and decide on the future course of action," Patil said."I was promised a ministerial post even before the 2023 Assembly polls, but during the government formation, I was told it would happen after 2.5 years. They failed to keep the promise. I have no other choice. I'm not quitting the party, but they have created an atmosphere compelling me to resign," he added.The expansion comes around two months after DK Shivakumar assumed office as chief minister and is expected to be one of the biggest reshuffles in the state.
Article Summary: DK Shivakumar: "Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay" Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned.

Article Title: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who probed Babri Masjid demolition, dies at 87
Article Text:
Justice MS Liberhan (Picture from Haryana govt website)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who headed the one-man commission that investigated the circumstances leading to the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, died on Sunday at the age of 87.Punjab and Haryana high court bar association President Rohit Sud confirmed his death, saying Justice Liberhan passed away in Chandigarh. His last rites will be held on Monday.Justice Liberhan began practising law at the Punjab and Haryana high court in 1964. He was elected to the Punjab and Haryana Bar Council in August 1970 and remained a member until February 11, 1987. During this period, he also served as the Bar Council's secretary from January 1976 to June 1983.He was elevated as a judge of the Punjab and Haryana high court on February 11, 1987. In July 1997, he was appointed Chief Justice of the Madras high court before taking over as Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh high court in February 1998.On December 16, 1992, days after the demolition of the Babri Masjid, the Centre appointed Justice Liberhan to head the one-man Liberhan Commission to probe the events leading up to the incident. The commission went on to become one of the longest-running inquiries in India's history.
Article Summary: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan died on Sunday at the age of 87. He headed the one-man commission that investigated the circumstances leading to the demolition of the Babri Masjid. The commission went on to become one of the longest-running inquiries in India's history.

Article Title: CRPF officer kills two colleagues, injures one before killing self in Assam
Article Text:
(Representative image)

NEW DELHI: A CRPF officer allegedly shot dead two of his colleagues and injured another before killing himself at a camp in Assam's Nagaon district on Tuesday, police told news agency PTI.The incident took place at the CRPF's 34 Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, at around 7 am, when Assistant Sub-Inspector (GD) Ballani Premabaram, who was on duty at the main gate, allegedly opened fire on his colleagues, Nagaon Deputy Superintendent of Police (HQ) Paramita Sarkar told PTI.Premabaram later turned the weapon on himself and died at the spot, she said.Head Constable (GD) Vishnu Prasad Baghel and Sub-Inspector (GD) Ramnawal Singh Yadav were killed in the firing, while Assistant Sub-Inspector (Mane) Govind Sripul was injured and admitted to a private hospital for treatment.
Article Summary: The incident took place at the CRPF's 34 Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon. Assistant Sub-Inspector Ballani Premabaram allegedly opened fire on his colleagues. He later turned the weapon on himself and died at the spot, police said.

Article Title: ‘Two sides of same coin’: Netaji’s grandnephew Chandra Bose quits TMC, takes swipe at BJP
Article Text:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the TMC on Monday, citing personal reasons, months after joining the party ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose on Monday resigned from the Trinamool Congress (TMC), saying he was "disillusioned" with mainstream political parties and saw "no difference" between the BJP and the Mamata Banerjee-led party.Bose, who joined the TMC barely four months ago ahead of the West Bengal assembly elections, said he would now mentor a proposed youth-led political platform based on the ideals of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose."I have been in the Forward Bloc, BJP and TMC. I am disillusioned with the mainstream political parties. They are all the same, just two sides of the same coin," Bose told PTI.He said the proposed platform would seek to offer an alternative to what he described as the politics of polarisation and confrontation."My politics is based on Netaji's ideology. We want to build a new political platform based on his principles of inclusive nationalism, secularism, social justice and development. I will mentor the youth who are coming together to form a party based on Netaji’s ideals," he added.There was no immediate reaction from the TMC to Bose's resignation.His exit marks another political shift for the former BJP state vice-president, who has repeatedly maintained that his politics is rooted in Netaji's ideology rather than party affiliation.Bose was earlier associated with the Forward Bloc, the party founded by Netaji. He joined the BJP in 2016 as the party expanded its political presence in West Bengal. He was subsequently appointed the party's state vice-president and contested the 2016 Assembly election and the 2019 Lok Sabha polls on a BJP ticket.His ties with the BJP later deteriorated. He was dropped as state vice-president during an organisational reshuffle in 2020 and increasingly voiced differences with the party leadership.Bose quit the BJP in 2023, claiming that the party had not lived up to its promise of advancing the inclusive nationalist ideals championed by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Sarat Chandra Bose.When he joined the TMC in April this year, Bose had criticised his former party over what he described as divisive politics and said the BJP's approach was contrary to the spirit of the Constitution."When I joined the Bharatiya Janata Party, I was made to understand that I could work to promote the ideology of Sarat Chandra Bose and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, which is inclusive and secular. India, as per the Constitution, is a sovereign, democratic, socialist, secular republic," he had said while joining the TMC.He had also described his decision to join the BJP as a "mistake" and said he hoped the TMC would provide a platform to uphold constitutional values and inclusive politics.Monday's resignation signals a similar disenchantment with the TMC, with Bose now seeking to build a political platform centred on Netaji's principles.Bose's political moves have attracted attention because of his family connection to Netaji and his sustained efforts to bring the freedom fighter's political philosophy into contemporary politics. Though he has not emerged as a mass electoral figure, he has consistently advocated what he describes as Netaji's vision of an inclusive India.Outside electoral politics, Bose has also campaigned for the preservation of Netaji's legacy. As spokesperson of the Open Platform for Netaji, he has led efforts seeking the declassification of files relating to the freedom fighter and greater public access to archival records concerning his life and disappearance.
Article Summary: Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the Trinamool Congress (TMC) on Monday. He said he was "disillusioned" with mainstream political parties and saw "no difference" between the BJP and the Mamata Banerjee-led party. Bose joined the TMC barely four months ago ahead of the West Bengal assembly elections.

Article Title: MP Pappu Yadav attacked at home during presser
Article Text:
The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple.

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded at the New Delhi address of Independent MP Pappu Yadav Sunday after a man allegedly threw a slipper at him and another allegedly brandished a knife when he was holding a news conference.The accused, identified by sources as Sumit and Happy Sharma, are from Bulandshahr in UP. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happy’s role. They are verifying if Happy was the one who threw a slipper at the MP, and if Sumit, who runs a hardware shop, brandished a knife at the event.The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple. On July 31, Opposition MPs staged a skit outside Parliament to protest on the issue, during which Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket. MP Bansuri Swaraj complained to police Saturday on the matter.Sunday’s videos show someone throwing a slipper at Yadav. Moments later, chaos erupts and chairs fly as supporters rush to overpower the men, and police step in. Members of Yadav’s team displayed before reporters the slipper and a knife which, they alleged, were used in the attack.Yadav alleged that it was a planned attempt on his life. “When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result,” Zaid, MP Yadav’s media convener, claimed.Happy told reporters that the duo was “not carrying a knife or any other weapon. We were allowed inside only after a security check.” Police, however, have found a knife in Sumit's possession.Advocate Kanishk Arora, of Yadav’s legal team, said the MP had received death threats in the past several days, including videos on social media announcing cash rewards for killing him and threatening his family. “We had informed Delhi Police about the threats and sought enhanced security ahead of Sunday’s news conference. However, only three police personnel were deployed,” Arora said.
Article Summary: The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple. Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket in the skit. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happy's role.

"These are the people who traded our trust in them for mere ministerial berths," he said, lashing out at "poisonous snakes" which sell trust to "buy" power, a reference to Congress's decision to snap ties with DMK and ally with TVK.Maran's strongly worded rejoinder captured the lingering sense of betrayal within the Dravidian party over Congress's swift embrace of its rival after the national party went to the poll as DMK's ally and was fully backed by the latter on all key issues, including Rahul's leadership, in national politics through its years in office.BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament, even though govt has so far not taken any official step to revive the bill that was defeated by a united Opposition in the last session.DMK has anyway indicated its openness over the issue, saying it will take a call after studying the bill and insisting that the proposed law should not harm south India's interests.Rahul's comments are also a nod to the acknowledgement in Opposition camp of the possibility of DMK revising its stand on a bill which, opposition parties have alleged, will allow BJP-led governing alliance to reconfigure constituencies to its advantage for the 2029 Lok Sabha poll.Targeting Rahul, Maran added, "Those who come to Tamil Nadu and stay silent about Cauvery rights are traitors. Those who only talk about irregularities in the exam, rather than insisting on completely abolishing NEET are traitors. Those who condemn BJP's horse-trading but ignore TVK's disgusting horse-trading are merely continuing that betrayal."

Article Title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
Article Text:
The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters.

Want to lay down norms on use of graded force, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for the dropping of cases against student protesters, Supreme Court on Monday permitted Delhi and state govts to withdraw or close FIRs lodged during NEET paper leak protests in different parts of India and said these youngsters must be allowed to pursue their studies without the fear of getting prosecuted.The bench clarified its July 28 order in which it had stayed coercive action against student protesters but permitted police to proceed with the investigations. This had created an apprehension in the minds of students about the future consequences of the cases remaining live.The go-ahead came after solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that “govt is serious about honouring the commitment (given to CJP) on withdrawal of cases against student protesters. We are discussing the modalities of dropping cases”.However, Mehta said that FIRs registered during student protests against 2,738 people who had criminal antecedents – having been accused of rape, murder and child sexual abuse under Pocso Act — and had infiltrated the protests to indulge in violence and vandalism will not be dropped. The bench said the rider would apply to those accused of heinous and grave offences and not petty offences or political cases.Mehta said, “Those who were leading the protests are again in touch with govt to work out the modalities for dropping cases against genuine student protesters as withdrawal of cases may not be possible under the law.” The top court posted the matter for further hearing on Aug 18.CJI Kant was firm that student protesters must be freed from the fear of future prosecution. He said, “Parameters for students are altogether different. Their cases should be considered in a different manner so that they remain in the mainstream and their education is not disturbed.“The parents are spending their hard-earned money on their children’s education. We must not keep aside the expectations of the parents of these youngsters. If the children are unnecessarily dragged into such (police and court) processes, it is not going to serve any purpose,” the CJI said.The solicitor general agreed and said modalities for the withdrawal/dropping of cases against student protesters will be worked out soon. He added, “There will be some people who would like to keep the pot boiling — we must be very careful even while taking legal steps.”Justice Bagchi said that when the parties agree to it, the court can engender and enable the process so that the FIRs do not remain hanging over students’ heads.Senior advocate Vrinda Grover said both CJP leaders and other students are in talks with the SG and govt to chart out an agreed modality for the dropping of cases. She cited a Patna FIR registered against 142 people and 5,000 unknown persons, and said this appeared to be ‘catch all’ tactics to pick up anyone randomly in the future. A comprehensive mechanism needs to be evolved, she said.Justice Bagchi said, “There are many options. The prosecution can file a closure report, the public prosecutor can advise withdrawal of cases or we can quash the FIRs.”The CJI-led bench said that while the violence and police excesses would be investigated by an SIT, “we want to lay down comprehensive guidelines for the future on use of graded force, whether it should include pellet guns or not, after getting recommendations from the high-powered committee we intend to constitute”.Senior advocate Shyam Divan said the committee/commission should be headed by a retired CJI. The bench said getting a former CJI to head the committee is difficult, and it will be chaired by a former SC judge. It asked Delhi Police, Centre and states to file their responses to the petition and give their suggestions on the terms of reference of the committee.Senior advocate N Hariharan questioned how Delhi Police could identify 2,738 criminals among the protesters and said they must have used face recognition devices on all protesters and profiled them, which is a serious violation of privacy of the individuals guaranteed under Article 21.
Article Summary: Supreme Court permitted Delhi and state govts to withdraw or close FIRs lodged during NEET paper leak protests in different parts of India. The bench clarified its July 28 order in which it had stayed coercive action against student protesters but permitted police to proceed with investigations.

Article Title: Opposition toughens stand, washout of session likely
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Raising the possibility of Parliament's monsoon session being a washout, opposition Monday told govt that a discussion on the Ram temple donation issue and Union minister Amit Shah's statement on police's alleged crackdown on students are a must for the legislature to function normally. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called the absence of PM Narendra Modi and Shah from both Houses an "insult to democracy".Amid opposition's protest, a bill in Lok Sabha to replace an ordinance that increased the number of SC judges from 34 to 38 was passed without discussion, with parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju slamming opposition for not participating in the debate in both Houses and alleging outside that they were not allowed to speak.Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, amid the din, introduced the bankers' books evidence bill to replace a British-era law with the objective of including all forms of records maintained by banks, including digital and cloud-based, as admissible evidence in the court of law in sync with digital dependence of the banking system.Opposition's stand in Parliament, then later at BAC meetings, was indicative of the continued disruptions.Govt has given no assurances on the demands.At the BAC meeting, SP MP Dharmendra Yadav and Congress's Kodikunnil Suresh took the lead to demand a discussion on alleged donation theft at Ram temple in Ayodhya, with an intervention by PM. They were backed by Shiv Sena, NCP-SP and other opposition MPs. Opposition also demanded a statement by Shah on police action on students.Rijiju claimed there was no one in LS to guide Congress MPs. Opposition's demand is a separate issue. They must participate in discussions over the bills, he added. "Rahul Gandhi didn't even attend the House today. Congress has completely fallen apart. Such important bills are coming up but they are not participating," he said.Given the ongoing standoff in Parliament over opposition's twin demands, the BAC meeting indicated that the monsoon session may be headed towards a washout.Congress MP KC Venugopal said "Shah used to be very active in the previous sessions. Why is he not attending this session?" Opposition MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav, NK Premachandran, Mahua Moitra, Gurjeet Aujla, Deepender Hooda, Mansoor Khan, Manish Tewari, and Jebi Mather held a protest in Parliament complex on the temple issue.
Article Summary: Opposition demands discussion on alleged donation theft at Ram temple in Ayodhya. They also demand a statement by Amit Shah on police action on students. PM Narendra Modi and Amit Shah did not attend Parliament's monsoon session. Bill to increase number of SC judges passed without discussion.

Article Title: J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
Article Text:
Kulgam: Security personnel keep a vigil during an inspection of vehicles to maintain public safety following the recent terror attack in Anantnag, at Qaimoh, Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A suspect was arrested Monday in J&K’s Pulwama with a hand grenade, three “anti-national” posters and a mobile phone during a security overdrive spurred by last week’s killings of two migrant labourers in a terror attack in neighbouring Kulgam.Police identified the man as Tousef Ahmad Dar, a local, and booked him under several laws, including the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Authorities claimed Dar was spotted walking towards a checkpoint set up jointly by J&K police, Army and CRPF and began to flee after noticing the security forces. Dar was chased down by troopers and caught some distance away, the police said.“The police remain committed to maintaining peace and security and will continue to take firm action against individuals involved in anti-national and unlawful activities,” the police said in a statement.The checkpoint where Dar was spotted is one of many across Kashmir that have come up after the killings of the two migrant workers on July 31.Earlier, on July 23, a terrorist shot dead a J&K head constable, Ashiq Hussain Qureshi, in south Kashmir’s Anantnag. It was the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre that left 26 people, most of them tourists, dead on April 22 last year. The police said Lashkar-e-Toiba offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF) was involved in both the Kulgam and Anantnag attacks.On Monday, Kashmir IG VK Birdi reviewed security and ordered robust counter-insurgency measures. “He (Virdi) stressed seamless coordination among all agencies. The IGP also reviewed security for highways, rail tracks and stations across the Valley. He directed officers to place “dynamic nakas” and ensure enhanced foot patrolling, particularly at night, at vulnerable locations and inter-district boundaries,” a police spokesman said.
Article Summary: Tousef Ahmad Dar, a local, was arrested in J&K’s Pulwama with a hand grenade, three ‘anti-national’ posters and a mobile phone. Dar was chased down by troopers and caught some distance away, police said. Kashmir IG VK Birdi reviewed security and ordered robust counter-insurgency measures.

Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: BJP chief Nitin Nabin vows introspection after Kishor ends party's 30-yr hold
Article Text:
Nitin Nabin says BJP will introspect after losing Bankipur bypoll to Prashant Kishor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday said the party would undertake a "thorough introspection" after losing the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Bihar, where Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar to end the party's three-decade dominance in the constituency.Kishor won the bypoll by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Neeraj Kumar's 44,827 votes. The victory marked Kishor's first electoral win since launching the Jan Suraaj Party and came less than a year after the party failed to win a single seat in the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections.Reacting to the bypoll results, Nabin accepted the verdict and said the BJP would analyse the reasons behind its defeats.In a post on X, Nabin said, "We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections.We express our heartfelt gratitude to the people of Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat for expressing their faith in the Bharatiya Janata Party. We extend our warm congratulations to all the dedicated workers and office-bearers of the BJP for this victory.In Bapni Pur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness, and with renewed energy and determination, we will continue to go among the people and work tirelessly to further strengthen their trust."Bankipur had been one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions since 1995. The seat was represented first by BJP leader Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha and later by his son, Nitin Nabin, who held it for five consecutive terms before vacating it after his election to the Rajya Sabha, triggering the bypoll.In the 2025 Bihar Assembly election, Nabin had retained the seat by a margin of more than 50,000 votes, making Kishor's victory one of the biggest political upsets in the state ahead of the Assembly elections.The bypoll also marked Prashant Kishor's electoral debut. After years as a political strategist, he launched the Jan Suraaj Party with a campaign centred on education, employment and governance reforms. His victory gives the fledgling party its first electoral success.Earlier in the day, Kishor said the result carried a message beyond Bankipur."It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.Following the result, the Jan Suraaj Party posted on X, "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipur--this is your victory."Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary also congratulated Kishor on his victory."In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Shri Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people's decision," he said in a post on X.According to the Election Commission, the Bankipur bypoll recorded a voter turnout of 34.24 per cent.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin says party will undertake a "thorough introspection" after losing Bankipur bypoll. Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar to end the party's three-decade dominance in the constituency.

Article Title: SC: How can transgender ID cards be rendered invalid?
Article Text:
The Supreme Court has sought the government's response regarding the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act.

NEW DELHI: SC Monday sought govt's response on pleas alleging Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, attempts to erase benefits accruing to transgenders under the old law and impinge on their right to receive hormone treatment for bringing their bodies in sync with self-identified genders.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked if the amendments are to be implemented prospectively, how could the transgender identity cards, issued under the earlier provisions of the law, be rendered invalid?Senior advocates complained those who were midway through their hormone treatment are being denied the same as doctors are not ready to provide such treatment fearing prosecution under the new law. "The national portal for transgenders has been discontinued denying them many benefits," they alleged.

Senior advocates complained those who were midway through their hormone treatment are being denied the same. Article Title: 'Gen Z protest' may have aided Bankipur win: Prashant Kishor after BJP bastion falls
Article Text:
'Atmosphere created by Gen Z protests' may have helped Bankipur win, says Prashant Kishor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor on Monday said the nationwide Gen Z protests may have contributed to his victory in the Bankipur Assembly bypoll, where he ended the BJP 's three-decade dominance. Fresh from his electoral debut victory, Kishor ruled out joining any political alliance and said his party would continue to chart an independent course in Bihar politics.Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by more than 19,000 votes in Bankipur, a constituency the BJP had held since 1995. The bypoll followed the resignation of BJP national president Nitin Nabin after his election to the Rajya Sabha.Speaking to reporters after the result, Kishor said the atmosphere created by the recent Gen Z protests may have influenced the outcome."The atmosphere created by Gen Z protests" might have played a role in the result, Kishor said, adding, "But there is nothing to show that young electors had voted in large numbers in Bankipur. It is unfortunate, but that is the reality," referring to the voter turnout of less than 35 per cent.Rejecting speculation about joining any political alliance, Kishor said, "We shall have no alliance. Our alliance shall be with the people of Bihar. You should see that the people of Bankipur have voted for us, giving up on established parties."He said the victory was possible because he received support beyond Jan Suraaj's core supporters."I would like to thank my active supporters as well as those who backed me in the by-election, despite not being with Jan Suraaj. I received support from people in BJP, Congress and RJD, who were unhappy with the state of affairs in their party," he said.Kishor also described the verdict as a rejection of the Bihar government, saying it was "essentially against" chief minister Samrat Choudhary.The former political strategist said, "The mandate is essentially against chief minister Samrat Choudhary, against whom I have nothing personal, but who is detested by educated people of Bihar because of criminal antecedents and lack of qualifications."Calling the result a warning for the BJP leadership, Kishor said the verdict should serve as a wake-up call for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He argued that if Choudhary had been chosen because of caste considerations, he should be replaced with someone from the same community who had a "cleaner background".The bypoll had become a prestige contest for the BJP after Nitin Nabin vacated the seat. In the 2025 Assembly election, Nabin had retained Bankipur by a margin of more than 50,000 votes.A senior BJP leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, acknowledged that Kishor had capitalised on growing discontent among sections of the party's traditional support base."Prashant Kishor struck all the right notes. He tapped into the growing dissatisfaction among the upper castes by raising issues like the death after suspected rape of a NEET aspirant and the police encounter of Bharat Tiwari," the leader said.The BJP leader added, "The Gen Z protests highlighted our weakening support among the youth, especially the upper castes, who have been our core base. They had been unhappy over the controversial UGC regulations and, now, they have begun to feel that we are taking them for granted."Leaders of INDIA bloc parties also linked the result to the recent student-led protests.CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said, "It is an emphatic victory against the BJP. In the backdrop of Jantar Mantar protests, it does indicate a welcome shift in public mood."Congress spokesperson Suman Kumar Mallick said, "The people of Bankipur have given a clear message against the arrogance of power and an autocracy. If Parliamentary elections are held today, Modi government will definitely be voted out."RJD spokesperson Chitaranjan Gagan said, "More important than who won is the fact that the BJP lost. We are not dejected and will work with renewed vigour to ensure the overthrow of the NDA from Bihar as well as the Centre."Veteran socialist leader Shivanand Tiwary also linked the verdict to the wider student movement."What we saw recently, at Jantar Mantar, across Bihar and in other parts of the country, was far more spectacular than what took place in 1974. Students' activists of today are showing a far superior acumen than what was on display in our times," he said.
Article Summary: Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by more than 19,000 votes in Bankipur. He ruled out joining any political alliance and said his party would continue to chart an independent course in Bihar politics. The bypoll followed the resignation of BJP national president Nitin Nabin after his election to the Rajya Sabha.

Article Title: From 2025 washout to historic sweep: How Prashant Kishor put Jan Suraaj on Bihar's electoral map
Article Text:
Jan Suraj party workers celebrated the victory of Prashant Kishor in Bankipur assembly byelection results (Image/PTI)

From assembly setback to bypoll comeback

Why Bankipur mattered

From strategist to politician

Breaking a BJP fortress

Message to BJP leadership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A political milestone

NEW DELHI: Nearly nine months after Jan Suraaj failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections, party founder Prashant Kishor on Monday secured his first electoral victory. He won the high-profile Bankipur bypoll, giving the fledgling outfit its first-ever seat in the Bihar assembly.Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Sinha's 44,827, according to the Election Commission.The victory marks Kishor's first electoral success since entering active politics and gives Jan Suraaj its first-ever representation in the Bihar Assembly, offering fresh momentum to a political project that had suffered a crushing setback during its electoral debut last year.The Bankipur result represents a significant political recovery for Kishor, whose Jan Suraaj Party failed to win even a single seat in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections despite contesting more than 200 constituencies.Launched after nearly two years of statewide outreach through the Jan Suraaj padyatra, the party had positioned itself as an alternative to both the NDA and the Mahagathbandhan, focusing on governance reforms, education, employment, migration and corruption rather than traditional caste-based politics.However, the ambitious campaign failed to translate into electoral support.Following the defeat, Kishor publicly accepted full responsibility for the party's performance."We made an honest effort, but it was completely unsuccessful. There's no harm in admitting this. Forget about systemic change; we couldn't even bring about a change in power," he had said after the Assembly election results."There must have been some mistake in our efforts, in our thinking, in the way we explained things. If the public did not show faith in us, then the responsibility for that is completely mine. I take that responsibility 100 per cent on myself."As an act of atonement, Kishor also announced that he would observe a day-long silent fast, saying he had failed to convince the people of Bihar why they should support a new political alternative.At the same time, he ruled out stepping away from politics."I will work twice as hard as you've seen me work over the past three years. There's no question of backing down. There's no turning back until I fulfil my resolve to make Bihar better," he had said.The Bankipur bypoll attracted national attention because of the political stakes involved for both the BJP and Kishor.The election was necessitated after BJP state president Nitin Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha.For nearly three decades, Bankipur had remained one of the BJP's safest urban constituencies. Before Nitin Nabin represented the seat, it had been held by his father, Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha, making it one of the party's strongest bastions in Bihar.In the 2025 assembly elections, Nabin had retained the constituency comfortably by a margin of over 50,000 votes.For Kishor, however, the bypoll was much more than a contest for a single assembly seat.After Jan Suraaj's disappointing electoral debut, the election became a crucial test of whether the party could convert years of grassroots mobilisation into actual electoral success.The contest also marked Kishor's first direct electoral battle after years of shaping campaigns for other political leaders from behind the scenes.Long before entering electoral politics himself, Prashant Kishor had built a reputation as one of India's most influential political strategists.Through his organisation Indian Political Action Committee (I-PAC), he worked on election campaigns for leaders across the political spectrum, including Narendra Modi, Nitish Kumar, Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, MK Stalin, Jagan Mohan Reddy, Uddhav Thackeray and others.His success as an election strategist later brought him closer to Nitish Kumar, who appointed him as an adviser with cabinet rank after returning as Bihar chief minister in 2015.In 2018, Kishor formally joined the Janata Dal (United) and quickly rose to become the party's national vice-president.However, differences with Nitish Kumar over issues including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act eventually led to his expulsion from the JD(U) in 2020.After briefly attempting to revive the Congress through organisational reforms, Kishor shifted his focus entirely to Bihar.In October 2022, he launched the Jan Suraaj padyatra, travelling across the state to build what he described as a grassroots political movement that would eventually evolve into a full-fledged political party.Although the movement generated considerable public attention, it failed to produce electoral success in the 2025 assembly elections.The Bankipur bypoll now marks Kishor's first major political endorsement as a politician rather than as a strategist.The BJP mounted an extensive campaign to retain Bankipur, deploying senior leaders, ministers and organisational workers to preserve its long-standing hold over the constituency.Despite the party's efforts, Kishor succeeded in wresting away one of the BJP's safest seats.The result is significant not because it alters the numerical balance of power in the Assembly, but because it breaks the perception that Jan Suraaj remains merely a political movement without electoral backing.It also establishes Kishor as an elected legislator for the first time.Beyond the numerical gain of a single seat, the victory gives Jan Suraaj institutional legitimacy.The party will now have a formal voice inside the Bihar assembly and is expected to use the legislative platform to strengthen its organisational presence ahead of future elections.Political observers believe the result could encourage more leaders and workers to join the party while helping it build credibility among voters who were hesitant to back it after the 2025 assembly elections.Although one bypoll does not erase the disappointment of last year's electoral performance, it significantly changes the political narrative around Jan Suraaj—from that of an unsuccessful newcomer to a party capable of winning in one of Bihar's most politically significant constituencies.Even before the counting concluded, Kishor had described the bypoll as something larger than a contest for one assembly seat."It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.Jan Suraaj also celebrated the result on social media, writing on X: "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipur—this is your victory."The Bankipur bypoll does not change Bihar's political arithmetic overnight. The NDA continues to enjoy a comfortable majority in the assembly with 122 seats.However, politically, the result marks an important milestone.After years of being known as the strategist behind other leaders' victories and after suffering a disappointing electoral debut in 2025, Prashant Kishor has finally secured an electoral mandate of his own."I am also congratulating those who lost the election. This is a democracy; there are wins and losses in elections. But the Bankipur election was not an election to elect an MLA. This election was to decide on the BJP-NDA government and its leadership. The people of Bankipur have voted that the central leadership of the BJP should consider it and, in the interest of Bihar, hand over the power of Bihar to a good person," he declared after victory.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor won the high-profile Bankipur bypoll, giving the fledgling outfit its first-ever seat in the Bihar assembly. He defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Sinha's 44,827, according to the Election Commission. Jan Suraaj failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections.

Article Title: Karnataka expands cabinet, 20 netas take oath; DKS hits back on ministerial berth row

NEW DELHI: Twenty new ministers were inducted into the Karnataka government on Monday as chief minister DK Shivakumar expanded his Cabinet to its full strength, two months after taking office.The swearing-in ceremony took place at Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru after Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot approved the expansion.The Cabinet expansion increased the strength of the ministry to the sanctioned limit of 34, including the chief minister.Among those sworn in were PM Narendraswamy, Shivaraj Tangadagi, Rudrappa Lamani, KS Basavanthappa, B Nagendra, T Raghumoorthy, BZ Zameer Ahmed Khan, Rizwan Arshad, Santosh Lad, Madhu Bangarappa, Putturangashetty, SS Mallikarjun, Dr Ajay Singh, N Chaluvaraya Swamy, KM Shivalinge Gowda, HC Balakrishna, Gayathri Shanthegowda, Basavaraj Rayareddi, Vijayanand Kashappanavar and Laxman Savadi.The Congress high command also approved GS Patil as the new Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and AS Ponnanna as the Deputy Speaker. Saleem Ahmed was named Chairman of the Legislative Council, while Umashree was appointed Deputy Chairperson.Ahead of the ceremony, Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative assembly after being left out of the Cabinet.Patil claimed his name had been included in the list until Monday morning but was removed from the final list released by the party."I was promised a ministerial post even before the 2023 Assembly polls. Later, I was told it would happen after 2.5 years, but the promise was not kept. I have no other choice," he said.He added that he was not resigning from the Congress but felt compelled to step down as MLA, calling it an insult to the people of his constituency. His supporters also staged a protest in Bengaluru over his exclusion.Reacting to the disappointment among party legislators, Shivakumar urged them to remain patient."There are many MLAs. It is not possible to accommodate everyone. Earlier, I too missed out on a ministerial berth in Siddaramaiah's Cabinet. But didn't I become a minister later? Similarly, we will provide opportunities to everyone in the future," the chief minister said.He also said, "I request them to be patient. We will create opportunities for everyone."The expansion saw the return of several former ministers, including B Nagendra, who had resigned from the previous Siddaramaiah government in 2024 over allegations linked to the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam.Former Deputy chief minister Laxman Savadi and senior leader Zameer Ahmed Khan were also among those inducted.However, several senior Congress leaders from the previous government, including H C Mahadevappa, H K Patil, Dinesh Gundu Rao, K Venkatesh, M C Sudhakar and Laxmi Hebbalkar were not included in the new Cabinet.Gayathri Shanthegowda is the only woman inducted in the expanded ministry. Three children of former chief ministers are now part of the Cabinet: Yathindra Siddaramaiah, Madhu Bangarappa and Dr Ajay Singh.
Article Summary: 20 new ministers were inducted into the Karnataka government on Monday. Chief minister DK Shivakumar expanded his Cabinet to its full strength. Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday challenged BJP leaders to make their educational qualifications public after an RTI query was filed seeking details of the funding for his studies abroad.In a video message shared on social media, Dipke said he was ready to disclose all documents related to his education."I just saw that a BJP worker has filed an RTI against me. Article Title: Needs 'decoding': RSS leader Atul Limaye links CJP protest to 'subversion of democracy', Dipke hits back
Article Text:
RSS's Atul Limaye calls CJP protest an 'alternative politics' experiment, Dipke says RSS can't call others anti-national

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Atul Limaye has alleged that the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest over the NEET-UG paper leak evolved into an "experiment for alternative politics", claiming that several political, student, labour and civil society organisations joined the agitation to propagate the idea of "subversion of democracy through democratic means. "Addressing an ABVP event in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on July 30, Limaye said the protest should be "decoded" to understand its chronology, methodology, support system and ideological underpinnings. He also alleged that anti-Hindu and "anti-national" slogans were raised during the agitation and questioned how it transformed from a student-led protest into a broader political movement.During his address, Limaye said, "In Today's times, CJP agitation should be studied as a case study. This has now come to the knowledge of everyone, but this was A phenomenon going on for years now. And if we have to study this whole agitation, we will have to see its full chronology, methodology and what their support system is, and the innovative system which they used and the ideology behind it. Of we see chronology, Abhijit Dipke was from our Marathwada itself. When he launched CJP, he got tremendous following (on social Media), and when he came back to India, he came back on 6th June and did his agitation on 7th."Describing the course of the agitation, he added, "But he didn't receive the response which was expected. So, he roamed around the country from 7th to 19th. He started agitation in various cities of the country, or tried to start agitation, but even there did not get that kind of response. So, he started agitation, sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar from the 20th onwards, and gradually the face of the agitation got changed. "According to Limaye, the movement later drew the participation of student organisations, labour unions, human rights groups, women's organisations, farmers' bodies and other civil society groups.He said, "What kind of things happened after that which changed the face of this agitation? What kind of support system did attach to this agitation? We need to see which organisations and institutions got attached to this agitation, and this will give us an idea of what kind of support system. This agitation obviously involved the youth, the students of the country. And that is why several student organisations got attached to it. Among the prominent organisations which were leading the stage in this protest was All India Student Association (AISA). And the second such Association was SFI."He further said, "Some human rights organisations, many tribal organisations, women organisations like Pinjra Tod joined them. Many Muslim organisations, Christian organisations, some institutions working in the legal sector, environment sector, journalistic associations also joined them. Some farmers' associations joined them, as Samyukta Kisan Morcha and Bharatiya Kisan Union joined them."Invoking Italian philosopher Antonio Gramsci's theory of cultural hegemony, Limaye argued that the protest was aimed at challenging democratic institutions and cultural values while operating within democratic processes.He said, "Why did the opposition to Hindus arise from the stage? Why were leaders from several political parties seen on the stage, and how did it convert from a student protest to a political protest? It was not limited to Delhi, but expanded in all the states. For this, we have to decode Yogendra Yadav's remark, 'Democracy's future now will not be decided in Parliament but on streets, elections will not decide, resistance will. ' The cause of the protest was genuine, but who captured the movement? If we understand this, then we will understand this protest. There is a lot to learn. This protest was an experiment for an alternative politics."He added, "This theory states subversion of democracy through democratic means. This is well documented, and Italian scholar Gramsci gave the theory of cultural hegemony. He said that cultural hegemony needs to be destroyed for revolution. The deconstruction theory challenged Lord Ram and other figures. Alternative politics states that till there is a system, like our Parliamentary system, there cannot be revolution. All the systems, including the judiciary and police, need to be challenged."Claiming that such politics could be pursued either electorally or through weakening public faith in institutions, Limaye said, "There are two ways: one is election and the second is subversion of democracy through democratic means. There is infiltration in the judiciary, education system, and bureaucracy. Second is challenging the institutions and eroding faith in them. The results are so dangerous. Many police officers said the way the women were behaving, it was difficult to tolerate.The way they were dressed and the language they used, we were ashamed. This was an attempt to degrade the culture."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke rejected the allegations and said the RSS had no moral authority to describe others as anti-national. Responding to Limaye's remarks on Monday, Dipke referred to the period when the RSS was banned following Mahatma Gandhi's assassination.Abhijeet Dipke said, "People who murdered Mahatma Gandhi are calling us anti-national. The murderers of Mahatma Gandhi have no moral right to call anyone else anti-national. Nathuram Godse was the first anti-national."The CJP had led a 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The agitation was withdrawn on July 25 after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the organisation said it had received assurances on its other key demands.
Article Summary: RSS's Atul Limaye said the protest should be "decoded" to understand its chronology, methodology, support system and ideological underpinnings. He also alleged that anti-Hindu and "anti-national" slogans were raised during the agitation.

Article Title: 'Neither officer using excessive force, nor criminal protester should be protected': SC
Article Text:
SC said states can withdraw FIRs against student who participated in NEET protests

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday observed that "neither a police officer using excessive force nor a hardened criminal under the garb of a student protest should be protected. " These remarks came as it heard petitions related to the NEET-UG protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20.The apex court said states are free to close or withdraw FIRs registered against student protesters, provided it is done in accordance with law. The court also indicated that it may lay down guidelines on the use of pellet guns during protests.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified that the term "criminal antecedents" refers only to grave and heinous offences, addressing concerns that students booked in minor or political cases could be denied relief.During the hearing, the CJI stressed that the court wanted to strike a balance between protecting peaceful protesters and ensuring accountability for serious offenders."A police officer involved in excessive force should not be unduly protected. And it should not be that a hardened criminal under the garb of student protest is also getting protected," the CJI observed.On allegations that pellet guns were used during the protest, the CJI said the court was considering issuing guidelines."We would like to lay down a protocol on how it can be used," he said.The bench noted that petitions had been filed both by protesters alleging excessive police force and by police personnel claiming they were injured during the violence.Appearing for the Centre, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the court that the Union government remained committed to its assurance that cases against student protesters would not be pursued, except in cases involving serious criminal offences.He said FIRs against more than 2,700 people with antecedents involving grave and heinous offences would not be withdrawn, according to ANI.Mehta also said there had been a misunderstanding regarding the government's stand on the issue. "Barring those with criminal antecedents, the government is prepared to address the cases against the student protesters. Let them sit with the government. There are some people who want to keep the pot boiling so we have to be cautious about the legal advice," he said.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for some petitioners, urged the court to examine allegations of police excesses during the protest. He said the petitioners had submitted around 300 videos showing the alleged use of force."The videos are very shocking. We have given 300 videos to the court. Since directions have come from the top, the commissioner of police must look at all this," he said.He further submitted, "Ideally, we have identified un-uniformed individuals committing such police excess. A direction has to go to the Commissioner of Police and the RAF Director as to why police used pellet guns etc."Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi sought clarification on the expression "criminal antecedents", arguing that it should not include minor offences."These are students, somebody may have a driving violation or a petty offence, or due to a political case. The word criminal antecedent needs to be clarified," Singhvi said, according to Live Law.He urged the court to exclude petty offences and cases arising out of political protests from the definition. Last week, the apex court had indicated that it would constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the July 20 incident and directed authorities to preserve CCTV footage and other official records related to the protest.The hearing comes days after the Supreme Court declined an oral plea seeking suo motu cognisance of the police action during the 'Chalo Sansad' protest.The court had earlier observed that police excesses or a lathi charge could not be justified merely because an agitation was taking place and underlined that the right to peaceful protest is "absolutely guaranteed."The matter has now been listed for further hearing on August 18.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said states are free to close or withdraw FIRs registered against student protesters. Court also indicated that it may lay down guidelines on the use of pellet guns during protests. Centre said FIRs against more than 2,700 people with antecedents involving grave and heinous offences would not be withdrawn.

Article Title: Congress workers detained while protesting E20 fuel outside Gadkari's residence: Watch

Congress workers held during E20 fuel protest outside Gadkari's Nagpur residence

NEW DELHI: Police on Monday detained Congress workers protesting against the Centre's ethanol-blended fuel policy outside Union Minister Nitin Gadkari's residence in Nagpur."We condemn E20 being imposed on us. We will continue to fight," said youth congress leader Mehul Adwani.The protest march began at Chitnavis Park Square in Mahal and proceeded towards Gadkari's private residence in the same locality, with Youth Congress workers raising slogans against the use of E20 ethanol-blended fuel, calling it unviable.A heavy police presence was deployed near the Union minister's residence, with barricades erected along the route. He alleged that the Centre was promoting ethanol-blended fuel under pressure from US President Donald Trump.Kejriwal further claimed that India had "yielded" to Trump by agreeing to import ethanol from the United States and alleged that the government's continued push for E20 petrol pointed to a "hidden agenda".
Article Summary: Police detained Congress workers protesting against the Centre's ethanol-blended fuel policy. Congress has been targeting Gadkari over the nationwide rollout of E20 fuel. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Gadkar had maintained that E20 petrol was introduced after years of scientific testing.

Article Title: 'Do not befriend Kaafirs': Pakistani general levels terror allegations against India
Article Text:
Pakistan's military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry

Pakistan's military spokesperson, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, has sparked controversy after saying in a video that Muslims should not befriend "kaafirs" (non-believers), warning that those who do would no longer be considered among the faithful."Do not befriend kaafirs (non-believers) and leave the faithful. If you do that, there's a problem. Then you are not among the Muslims," Chaudhry said while addressing a press conference.“Now our population is 240-250 million people, and we still have four provinces. We have to see whether this is serving the purpose of good governance. That debate has to be sensibly held by politicians, by those in power, even those who have previously been in power, and those who are responsible to the people of Pakistan,” he added.The remarks were made during a wider media briefing that focused on Pakistan's counter-terrorism operations, the security situation in Balochistan, and the country's ties with Afghanistan.Taking a jibe at India-Afghanistan ties, Chaudhry claimed that the Afghan Taliban regime's "business" was terrorism, alleging that it used militancy to sustain its economy, state institutions and diplomacy.“Even their diplomacy is centred on terrorism. What is common between India and Afghanistan, except their DNA? The only thing common is terrorism,” Chaudhary said, as cited by Dawn.Chaudhry also claimed that around 300 Indian websites were being used to support terrorism-related activities in Balochistan, while more than 1,000 social media accounts and what he described as a "hostile diaspora" were involved in spreading propaganda linked to terrorism.“First, an event or incident is seeded, right or wrong, and then it is framed by initiators, who hand it over to amplifiers. Then mass amplification is done by mainstream Indian media, channels and their print media as well, from where it is picked up by international media, and then you take it and run it as facts," he said.The DG ISPR said the government was also working to strengthen the police force, including by deploying newly recruited assistant superintendents of police (ASPs) to Balochistan and providing bulletproof vehicles, among other measures.The remarks come amid a series of attacks on Pakistani security forces across Balochistan last month, with armed clashes also reported during military operations in the Mastung and Kech districts, according to The Balochistan Post (TBP).The insurgency in Balochistan has been led by several separatist groups, including the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), which has waged a long-running campaign against Pakistan's federal government. The group has frequently targeted security personnel and infrastructure in the province and has also carried out attacks in other parts of the country, including Karachi.According to Pakistan's 2023 census, Balochistan is home to around 15 million people and is rich in natural resources, including coal, gold, copper and natural gas. The BLA maintains that these resources should belong to the people of Balochistan and opposes the federal government's control over their extraction and the province's security.
Article Summary: Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Muslims should not befriend "kaafirs" (non-believers) He warned that those who do would no longer be considered among the faithful. The remarks were made during a wider media briefing on Pakistan's counter-terrorism operations.

Article Title: Unhappy over non-inclusion in Karnataka Cabinet, 2 Congress MLAs resign
Article Text:
Two Congress MLAs, Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (R) and Belur Gopalakrishna (L), resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Monday





BENGALURU: Two Congress MLAs resigned from the Karnataka Legislative assembly on Monday after they were left out of the state cabinet expansion.Indi MLA Yashavantarayagouda V Patil and Sagar MLA Belur Gopalakrishna announced their resignations ahead of the swearing-in ceremony for the new ministers.Patil handed his resignation to deputy speaker Rudrappa Lamani at Vidhana Soudha.Soon after, his supporters staged a protest in Bengaluru, alleging that he had been treated unfairly.Gopalakrishna also resigned from the Assembly, increasing pressure on the Congress leadership as it prepared for the cabinet expansion.Later speaking to reporters, Patil said his name was on the list until this morning, and he had even received intimation, but it did not figure in the final list released by the party."I have been watching the developments within the party; ultimately today, during the expansion, our leadership failed to keep the promise made. So, without any other option, it was inevitable for me to resign. I have submitted the resignation," he said.Clarifying that he was not quitting for the sake of position, Patil said, "It is not acceptable to my conscience. The situation in Vijayapura district is that loyalty and honesty are not valued in the Congress party.I have no other choice. I will speak to my supporters and well-wishers and decide on the future course of action.""I was promised a ministerial post even before the 2023 assembly polls, but during the government formation, I was told it would happen after 2.5 years, but they failed to keep the promise. I have no other choice. I'm not quitting the party, but they have created an atmosphere compelling me to resign," he said.Describing himself as a "mature politician" who has faced eight elections, he asserted, "I never back down from my decisions; this is an insult to the voters of my constituency."The Congress government is set to induct 20 ministers into the state cabinet, with the oath-taking ceremony scheduled for 5pm at Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru.The expansion comes about two months after D K Shivakumar took charge as chief minister.The resignations are likely to deepen dissatisfaction within the party, with several leaders reportedly unhappy over being left out of the new cabinet.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Indi MLA Yashavantarayagouda V Patil and Sagar MLA Belur Gopalakrishna announced their resignations ahead of the swearing-in ceremony for the new ministers. Patil handed his resignation to deputy speaker Rudrappa Lamani at Vidhana Soudha. His supporters staged a protest in Bengaluru, alleging that he had been treated unfairly.

Article Title: Delhi riots 2020: Why Tahir Hussain escaped death penalty in IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
Article Text:
Why the court awarded life imprisonment instead of death

Prosecution sought death penalty

Defence argued case did not qualify as 'rarest of rare'

Court's conviction order

Murder during Delhi riots

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots, rejecting the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh pronounced the sentence after hearing arguments from both the prosecution and the defence on the quantum of punishment. The court said the prosecution had not established that the case met the threshold for awarding capital punishment, even though it had convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder earlier this month.The judgment was delivered in the physical presence of Hussain and the other convicts amid tight security at Delhi's Karkardooma Court.While the Delhi Police had argued that the case fell within the "rarest of rare" category warranting capital punishment, the court concluded that the prosecution had not proved that the convicts were incapable of reform, a key principle laid down by the Supreme Court for awarding the death penalty.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh observed that the prosecution was unable to establish that the convicts were beyond reformation, leading the court to impose life imprisonment instead.The prosecution had sought the death penalty for Hussain and the four co-convicts, arguing that the murder was brutal, deliberate and carried out without any provocation.During the sentencing hearing, Special Public Prosecutor Madhukar Pandey described the crime as "anti-social and abhorrent" and argued that it qualified as one of the "rarest of rare" cases.Pandey told the court that Sharma was subjected to a cold-blooded and savage attack with a heavy cutting weapon and that the killing could not be viewed in isolation because it occurred during the northeast Delhi riots in which 53 people lost their lives.According to the prosecution, Sharma sustained 51 injuries, seven of which were independently sufficient to cause death.The prosecution further submitted that the convicts acted without provocation and displayed complete disregard for the consequences of their actions.Earlier, Pandey had argued that the accused had fallen to the "level of being animals" while assaulting Sharma and said:"Those who are asking for mercy today should have shown mercy themselves. No mercy was shown from anyone's side. No one even took Ankit to the hospital. They are asking for mercy after committing such a brutal murder."The prosecution also argued that Hussain, being an elected municipal councillor at the time, had a greater responsibility to protect citizens instead of becoming part of the unlawful assembly.The defence, however, urged the court to show leniency, arguing that not every murder warranted capital punishment and that aggravating and mitigating circumstances must both be considered.Senior advocate Rajiv Mohan, appearing for Hussain, argued that six of the eleven accused in the case had already been acquitted and that the prosecution had failed to establish any conspiracy during the trial.The defence maintained that Hussain's conviction rested on his membership of an unlawful assembly and common intention rather than evidence showing he personally inflicted fatal injuries on Sharma.The counsel further argued that there had been no preparation or conspiracy, that Sharma had been attacked by a large crowd during widespread rioting and that Hussain's conduct during custody had remained satisfactory.Advocate Tara Narula also urged the court to consider Hussain's family circumstances, submitting that he had three children, an elderly father and that his wife was a homemaker dependent on rental income.Counsel representing the other convicts similarly pleaded for leniency, citing their family responsibilities and arguing that both communities had been involved in the violence.The court, however, rejected several of the defence's contentions before pronouncing the sentence.On July 13, the court convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder.In its conviction order, the court held that Hussain was a member of a heavily armed mob that had assembled with animus against Hindus to commit rioting, arson and looting before murdering Sharma in what it described as a "savage and relentless assault."The court further held that the prosecution had proved members of the unlawful assembly knew that pursuing their common object could result in death.Ankit Sharma, an Intelligence Bureau officer, was killed during the northeast Delhi riots in February 2020 in the Dayalpur area. His mutilated body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was convicted under Sections 302 (murder), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person), 147 (rioting), 148 (rioting armed with a deadly weapon), 153A (promoting enmity) and 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 149 relating to unlawful assembly.With Friday's sentencing order, Hussain and the four co-convicts will serve life imprisonment, while the court's decision underscores that despite the brutality of the crime, the legal threshold required for imposing the death penalty was not met because the prosecution failed to prove they were beyond the possibility of reformation.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots. The court rejected the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.

Her alarm drew neighbours, who informed police.While residents alleged that the girl had been sexually assaulted before being killed, police said they will wait for the autopsy report before ascertaining the exact cause of death and whether the victim had been an assaulted or not.Hailakandi SP Amitabh Sinha and senior district officials inspected the scene, before meeting the victim’s family, assuring them of a fair and expeditious investigation.The incident triggered protests, with residents blocking NH-6, which connects Hailakandi with Mizoram , to demand the immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible. US President Donald Trump on Sunday claimed that the United States had been "locked and loaded" with military force against Iran at levels "not seen since World War II" but said he decided to call off the planned attack after Tehran and several Middle Eastern countries urged to hold off and pushed to make a deal.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said Iran had requested that Washington "hold off any attack" after the broad parameters of an agreement had been reached. NEW DELHI: Responding to remarks by exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said comparisons between the group's protests and student movements in Bangladesh and Nepal were misplaced."Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," Dipke told PTI.Nasreen had on Sunday drawn parallels between the CJP-led protests in Delhi over alleged examination irregularities and the 2024 student-led movement in Bangladesh that led to the fall of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's government.She said the student movement in Bangladesh had "fooled us".In a separate development, CJP extended support to students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand, as a student leader began an indefinite hunger strike demanding an independent investigation into the recruitment process.Dipke said he spoke to student leaders through a video call on Sunday night and backed their demands. Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor
