GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya , who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: A stalker walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name. He then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent. The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village infaridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours.

Article Title: Udhayanidhi Stalin detained from Chennai home over 'vulgar' remarks against actor Trisha
Article Text:
Udhayanidhi Stalin faced detention after a case was registered against him

Poll Vote & Share your view Should political leaders be more careful with public statements? Yes, words matter No, open debate is important 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





CHENNAI: DMK leader and leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin was detained from his residence in Neelankarai on Tuesday after a case was registered against him over his allegedly objectionable remarks made during a rally on the Cauvery water dispute in Thanjavur.A police team led by Joint Commissioner of Police Dr P Vijayakumar took Udhayanidhi into custody from his residence and escorted him in a police vehicle. He will be taken to Thanjavur, where the FIR was registered in connection with his speech at Monday's rally on the Cauvery water dispute.The detention came after Udhayanidhi moved the Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail, apprehending arrest in the case. When the matter was mentioned before Justice G K Ilanthiraiyan, the court agreed to hear the urgent plea and orally directed the police not to precipitate the issue until the petition was taken up.Speaking to reporters after being detained, Udhayanidhi dismissed the case as "forged" and said he would fight it legally. He alleged that since the TVK government came to power, it had been filing "fake cases" against DMK MLAs and indulging in "horse-trading."During the rally, sections of the crowd began chanting "Trisha, Trisha". After pausing briefly, Udhayanidhi allegedly remarked, "Whether the water reaches anywhere else or not, it should reach there," before adding that he was referring to the Cauvery water.The controversy erupted after the remarks, with opposition parties accusing the DMK leader of making a double-entendre comment targeting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay while responding to slogans raised by party workers.Based on a complaint filed by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), Thanjavur police registered an FIR against Udhayanidhi under charges of promoting enmity between groups, provisions of the Information Technology Act, and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.TVK also approached the National Commission for Women (NCW), alleging that Udhayanidhi's remarks were "vulgar", "objectifying" and "sexually suggestive". In its complaint, the party sought legal action against the DMK leader, an unconditional public apology and intervention by the commission.TVK national spokesperson Pazha Selvakumar alleged that the remarks objectified women, undermined the dignity of women in public life and lowered the standards of political discourse. The party urged the NCW to examine the video footage of the speech and recommend action for alleged public obscenity and outraging the modesty of women.
Article Summary: DMK leader and leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin was detained from his residence in Neelankarai on Tuesday. A case was registered against him over his allegedly objectionable remarks made during a rally on the Cauvery water dispute in Thanjavur. He dismissed the case as "forged" and said he would fight it legally.

Article Title: West Bengal police bust drug network, seize Rs 2.5 crore cash, cough syrup and gold; 3 arrested
Article Text:
Three people were arrested following the raid at a flat in Mangalbari area of Malda district, officials said.





KOLKATA: Around Rs 2.5 crore in cash, thousands of bottles of banned cough syrup and a small quantity of gold were seized during an overnight raid in West Bengal's Malda district as part of a probe into an anti-cold drug smuggling racket, police said on Monday.Three people were arrested following the raid at a flat in Mangalbari area of Malda district, officials said according to news agency PTI.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said the operation had dealt "a massive blow to an interstate and cross-border drug network", asserting that his government remained committed to its zero-tolerance approach against criminal activities.The joint operation was carried out by police teams from Dakshin Dinajpur and Malda districts with assistance from the state police's Special Operations Team. The raid followed the arrest of alleged smuggler Mridul Ghosh last month.Based on leads gathered during the investigation, police arrested Ghosh's alleged associate Pintu Sarkar and two other accused, an official said.Reacting to the development, the chief minister said,"Our government maintains an absolute 'zero tolerance policy' against drugs, crime and illegal syndicates. West Bengal will remain steadfast in protecting its youth and ensuring that our soil is never used by criminal networks."In a post on X, Adhikari said the joint operation had dealt "a massive blow to an interstate and cross-border drug network" and praised the Dakshin Dinajpur and Malda district police for carrying out the raid.According to Adhikari, police recovered Rs 2.4 crore in cash, thousands of bottles of banned cough syrup worth around Rs 90 lakh in the black market, and approximately 20 grams of gold."Interrogations (of the arrested accused) are underway to unearth the entire nexus and root out every single individual connected to this racket," Adhikari said.He said raids were continuing in border areas and warned that there would be no mercy for those involved in drug trafficking.Police officials said the investigation was underway to trace the source of the seized cash, establish ownership of the premises and identify other people linked to the alleged smuggling network.
Article Summary: Three people were arrested following the raid at a flat in Mangalbari area of Malda district, officials said. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said the operation had dealt "a massive blow to an interstate and cross-border drug network"

AHMEDABAD: As many as 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus (CHPV) in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 cases testing positive out of 184 suspected infections, state health minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.Seven patients remain under treatment across civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Rajkot and other districts, news agency PTI reported.Government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to immediately admit symptomatic patients to ICU beds to prevent organ failure, Panseriya said."A total of 184 suspected cases have been registered in the state so far, out of which 35 cases have tested positive and the results of 11 samples are still pending," he informed.Out of the cases reported so far, 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus, he said.All patients are under 15 years of age, he added.Children admitted to civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are being provided the best and super-specialist treatment, with doctors monitoring their condition, Panseriya said.He further noted that cases are being reported from different areas and are not concentrated in a particular village.Health teams are spraying pesticides in areas where animal husbandry is practised to target sandflies, which are responsible for spreading the encephalitis virus, PTI reported.Government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to admit patients showing symptoms of the virus to ICU beds with oxygen and ventilator facilities and not delay treatment so that serious conditions such as multiple organ failure can be prevented, he said.Chandipura encephalitis is a viral disease that spreads mainly through sandflies and other insects and causes inflammation of the brain.The virus was first isolated from a patient in Chandipura village in Nagpur district of Maharashtra in 1965.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: As many as 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus (CHPV) in Gujarat this monsoon season. 35 cases testing positive out of 184 suspected infections, state health minister Praful Panseriya said. Seven patients remain under treatment across civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Rajkot and other districts.

Article Title: Visa extension filed? Immigration attorney says ICE can still arrest you; Oakland's Chantal Morales Rojas also did her paperwork before deadline
Article Text:
Filing an extension before visa expiry may not save you from ICE arrest.

What is the case of Chantal Morales Rojas?

Amid a sudden spike in arrests at domestic airports, immigration lawyer Poonam Gupta said what is happening is not a fault of the visa holders; it is assumptions going wrong. Citing the recent case of Oakland's Chantal Morales Rojas who was arrested on the accusation of visa overstay, Gupta said Rojas came to the US legally on a J-1 visa as an au pair. Before it expired, she timely filed an extension application, but that did not stop ICE officials from detaining her. And she was released only after a court order.Gupta urged visa holders not to assume that they won't be detained just because they filed an extension for their visa on time and becaue they do not have any criminal record."A timely-filed extension or status application legally starts a period of authorized stay. ICE is arresting people anyway. At airport check-in counters and gates, including travelers with pending green card, asylum, and extension applications, at least 27 arrests across 15 airports in 9 states in recent weeks, per an internal DHS memo obtained by ABC News," Gupta wrote in a LinkedIn post."Two things people assume protect them. Right now, neither reliably does: A pending extension application: legally, this starts authorized stay; A domestic flight: no border, no customs, should be lower risk," she explained."This isn't a loophole or a technicality — it's the law working as intended, and ICE treating it as if it doesn't," she said urging visa holders to consult their immigration attorneys before booking domestic flights.Chantal Morales Rojas, an Oakland resident originally from Ecuador, took part in a short group trip to Denver for a frisbee tournament but she was stopped, questioned and then arrested on the jetway of her flight home on July 20. The administration said she was detained as she overstayed her visa that expired on January 4, 2025. She was taken to the GEO Detention Facility in Aurora, Colorado, while her friends started raising money for legal help.Last week, Rojas was released on a $3,000 bond.Rojas filed an extension of her visa before it expired but it remained pending at the time of her arrest.
Article Summary: Immigration lawyer Poonam Gupta says visa holders' assumptions are going wrong. She urged visa holders not to assume that they won't be detained just because they filed an extension for their visa on time. A timely-filed extension or status application legally starts a period of authorized stay, Gupta said.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's call for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest has triggered a fresh response, with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioning whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words.Reacting to the Prime Minister's selfie-style Instagram video, Dipke wrote, "Fraand, sirf reel par hi maaf karoge ya cases bhi wapas loge?(Friend, will you forgive them only through reels, or will you also withdraw the cases?)"The Prime Minister's video, shared on his official Instagram and X handles on Friday, came after a 15-year old protester from Noida was booked for allegedly using derogatory language against him during at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In the video, PM Modi said, "Today I just feel like talking to you. The country and the world have witnessed what happened at Jantar Mantar. Some mischievous children used very crude and abusive language, words that do not befit any civilized society. I was personally abused, and even my late mother was subjected to abuse. It was a truly ugly spectacle."Acknowledging the public outrage over the incident, the Prime Minister urged people to view the matter through the lens of reform rather than punishment.He said that while the students' remarks had understandably outraged society, mistakes are part of growing up. He urged people to forgive them, guide them in the right direction, and help them reform, saying the students had "lost their way" but deserved an opportunity to correct themselves.The Prime Minister further argued against prolonged legal action and social ostracisation."Punishing them, dragging them through court proceedings, and harassing them in society, none of this will change the situation. I want to forgive them. Society, too, should accept this," PM Modi said, while urging the students to learn from their mistakes and move forward.Earlier, Dipke had questioned the police action and alleged selective enforcement of the law.In a video shared by CJP on X, he said, "If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT Cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?"He further alleged that several social media users identifying themselves with the BJP had routinely targeted women online."They have been using all kinds of words, not respecting women from any angle. And they proudly wrote in their bio, 'Followed by PM Modi'. Such people have abused girls. When will the case be filed on them?" Dipke said.Questioning the criminal proceedings, Dipke argued that abusive language, while objectionable, should not automatically attract criminal prosecution."If cases are to be filed for abusing, highest number of cases will be filed against the BJP's IT Cell, because they are the ones who have abused women the most. And it will be against BJP's leaders, who have used bad language for years, even inside the Parliament," he said.In a post accompanying the video, CJP asked, "Will an FIR be filed against all those IT Cell members who have been abusing women for the last several years?"This is not the first time Dipke has publicly reacted to one of the Prime Minister's social media videos. Earlier on Thursday, after PM Modi released a video message highlighting the recently passed anti-paper leak legislation, Dipke commented on Instagram, "Your skin is brighter than the country's future."The Prime Minister had described the legislation as a key reform aimed at strengthening the examination system.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi's call for compassion towards students accused of abusing him at the Jantar Mantar protest has triggered a fresh response. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned whether the message of forgiveness would extend beyond words.

Article Title: 'Enjoys playing victim card': Congress attacks PM Modi's 'forgive youth' remark
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth.He said the Prime Minister should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "The self-declared non-biological PM enjoys playing the victim card." He further alleged that the Prime Minister "uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents" and "very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself.""He uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents. He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection," Ramesh said.Referring to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and student protests, Ramesh said, "the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors."He also said the Prime Minister owed an apology over the "Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka by the Ram Mandir Trust" and for the "Tughlakian notebandi of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs."Ramesh added, "but late last night, in act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth." He alleged that the remark was "an insult to the nation and to our youth", adding that young people had suffered under the government's policies and were instead seeking an apology from the Prime Minister."The Prime Minister’s InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one," Ramesh added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared a video late at night that carried a message against abusive language and hate, saying "abuses never solve anything," amid a controversy over alleged derogatory remarks made against him by a woman from Noida during a protest in Delhi."Abuses never solve anything. Let’s guide the misguided. Let’s work together. Let’s work for Bharat," PM Modi wrote, sharing the video on X.In the video, PM Modi also highlighted the government's efforts to strengthen the country's examination system, citing Parliament's passage of a stringent anti-paper leak law."Friends, we are continuously taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. Whether it is creating fast-track mechanisms or incorporating suggestions from the states, we are working in that direction."The Prime Minister said paper leaks had affected governments across the country for decades and jeopardised the future of students.PM Modi reiterated that the government would act firmly against those involved in paper leak rackets.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth. He said the PM should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.

Article Title: Bhiwandi crash: Buiding owner, repairs contractor booked; state orders probe
Article Text:
A five-storey Bhiwandi building collapsed, killing ten people and injuring three others

Hundreds of dangerous buildings in MMR, thousands at risk (Photo credit: Santosh Gupta)





MUMBAI: The state govt ordered an inquiry into the crash of a part of a five-storey Bhiwandi building that claimed 10 lives.An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) of BNS and relevant provisions of Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act for illegal construction, said DCP (zone 2), Thane, Pawan Basod.The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed and the CM Rs 5 lakh each.This was the third such major building collapse in Bhiwandi since 2020.Repairs began four days earlier after residents flagged falling plaster chunks and hired a contractor on their own. The building was not vacated during the work.Around 8pm on Thursday, residents noticed that a supporting pillar in wing B had developed a crack and was tilting, alerted the contractor and vacated the building.Workers were immediately brought in and the pillar was reinforced with iron support rods. Assuming that the structure had been stabilised, many residents went back into the building around 11.30pm.Moments later, half the wing collapsed, trapping many residents and labourers under the rubble.Over the next 15 hours, NDRF, fire brigade and Thane disaster response force personnel pulled out the bodies of Rakesh Paswan (25), Mukesh Paswan (30), Ashok Paswan (40), Krish Kumar (32), Ranjit Singh (45), Radheshyam Kushwaha (45), Siraj Rasul Sheikh (45), Shamim Ansari (32), Shyam Pal (40), and Santosh Pandey (42).Those injured, Abhay Yadav (26), Deepak Yadav (25) and Sangeeta Prajapati (36), were taken to a hospital. Some residents were rescued from the portion of the wing that remained standing.An NDRF officer said the building suffered a “pancake collapse”, in which one floor falls directly onto another.“The chances of survival in such collapses are extremely low. We deployed trained sniffer dogs to locate the victims.”Disaster management minister Girish Mahajan, who visited the site, said the repairs were carried out late at night to escape civic scrutiny.He directed the authorities to ensure that all dangerous buildings in Bhiwandi are vacated and appropriate action.Mehtab Ansari, a resident, told TOI that all flat owners had contributed around Rs 10,000 each for the repairs.Another resident, Komal Arvind Gupta, alleged that negligence during the work damaged the pillar.
Article Summary: An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed.

Article Title: Spain says most migrants return to Morocco after border rush kills 57
Article Text:
As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds

Spain said on Friday that it had regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returning to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 migrants entered Ceuta between Thursday and Friday, with about 48,300 having already returned to Morocco by Friday evening. Ceuta regional president Juan Jesus Vivas, however, estimated that the total number of crossings could have reached 60,000 over the two days.As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds and prevent more people from entering the Spanish territory.Reuters reporters at the scene also saw riot police firing tear gas, while water cannon vehicles were deployed to disperse migrants. Burnt remains of a bus and seven cars were visible following clashes.On the Spanish side, military vehicles were positioned along sections of the border as hundreds of migrants remained stranded on the Moroccan side. Several hundred people later crossed back through official checkpoints and openings in the fence, with many saying they were unable to find food or shelter in Ceuta. "I'm going back," one migrant told news agency Reuters.Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday, where he faced protests and jeers from demonstrators. He described the mass border crossing as "a violation of Spain's territorial sovereignty" and said authorities were accelerating the return of those who had entered illegally with Morocco's full cooperation.The incident also exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy. Italy announced it was temporarily suspending the European Union's Schengen border-free travel arrangements with Spain, a decision that would affect air and sea travel between the two countries. Madrid criticised the move, saying it breached European Union treaties.Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's two autonomous enclaves in North Africa, form the European Union's only land borders with Africa. While both regularly witness attempts by migrants to enter Europe, Spanish authorities described the latest influx as unprecedented.Several right-wing political parties across Europe blamed the crisis on Spain's migration policies, including this year's amnesty for hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants. Spain also summoned the Italian ambassador after Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani claimed the amnesty had "encouraged human trafficking".US President Donald Trump also weighed in on the crisis, describing the situation at Ceuta as an invasion.The crossings "look like an invasion", Trump said, adding, "That same thing's going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected, except worse," referring to the upcoming US midterm elections.The US state department also criticised Spain's handling of migration, saying the incident was "the direct result of the Spanish Government's deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe." It added, "We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar option."Meanwhile, France said it would significantly strengthen security along its border with Spain.French interior minister Laurent Nunez announced that the police presence would be increased fivefold by Saturday, alongside enhanced aerial surveillance and additional patrols on trains.Spain's Guardia Civil police association AUGC also criticised the handling of the situation, saying there had been too few officers deployed at the border fence during the surge, leaving security forces unable to stop the mass crossings.
Article Summary: Spain says it has regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta. Most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returned to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.

Article Title: 4.7-magnitude earthquake hits Italy; buildings damaged, four injured
Article Text:
4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four (Reuters image)

A 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck the volcanic Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields) area near the southern Italian city of Naples on Friday, injuring four people, damaging buildings and churches. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.The earthquake struck at 7.46 pm (local time), with its epicentre in the Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km (2 miles), according to Italy's National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.The Italian fire service said minor damage was reported to buildings in and around Naples, but added that emergency crews had not received any immediate requests for rescue or assistance, as cited by Reuters.As a precaution, local authorities suspended rail and metro services while inspections were carried out.Italian media described the tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded in the Campi Flegrei area, prompting residents in several neighbourhoods to rush onto the streets as the ground shook.Campi Flegrei, a densely populated volcanic caldera that spans much of western Naples, has witnessed increasingly frequent seismic activity in recent years, prompting Italian authorities to intensify monitoring of the area.While low-intensity tremors are common in the region, stronger earthquakes have revived concerns over a repeat of the seismic crisis of the early 1980s, which caused widespread disruption and forced thousands of residents to evacuate their homes.Italy is prone to earthquakes due to its geological setting. In 2016, a series of powerful quakes struck central Italy, devastating parts of the Lazio, Umbria and Marche regions and killing around 300 people.The country's deadliest earthquake in recent decades was the 6.9-magnitude Irpinia quake in southern Italy in November 1980, which claimed about 2,700 lives and devastated hundreds of towns.
Article Summary: 4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four people. Epicentre in Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km. Italian media described tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded.

Article Title: US Marine F-35 fighter jet crashes in San Diego, pilot ejects safely
Article Text:
Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

A US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday, with the pilot ejecting safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire, military officials said.The fighter aircraft, attached to the 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing and Marine Aircraft Group 11, went down at around 10 am local time near the air station. The Marine Corps described the incident as an "aircraft mishap".First Lieutenant Blake Starbuck told Fox News that the crash was a "Class A mishap involving a Marine Corps F-35B in the vicinity of MCAS Miramar".Lieutenant Starbuck confirmed that the pilot successfully ejected and was safely recovered after the aircraft came down. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.Starbuck said he could not immediately confirm the purpose of the flight, including whether the aircraft had been taking off, landing or carrying out a training mission.He also said there was no immediate information about any injuries or fatalities linked to the crash.Television footage from SkyRanger 7 showed the wreckage split into two large sections in the middle of a burnt field roughly the size of a football pitch.Large flames and thick black smoke rose from the crash site, which was located north of State Route 52, making the fire visible to motorists on the nearby highway. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department said it had joined efforts to contain the brush fire triggered by the crash.However, officials said the military remains in charge of the crash site and will lead the investigation into the incident.
Article Summary: US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday. Pilot ejected safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

Article Title: This 44-year-old Swedish man survived being buried beneath a metre of snow for nearly two months against all odds
Article Text:
Image: Left/The Telegraph/Right/The Guardian

Snowmobilers uncovered the buried car after noticing something unusual beneath the snow

Doctors believed melted snow and an extremely slow metabolism helped keep him alive

The case challenged assumptions about the limits of human survival

One of the most remarkable modern survival stories

In December 2011, a 44-year-old Swedish man named Peter Skyllberg disappeared while driving through the country's frozen north. Weeks passed with no sign of him as winter temperatures plunged well below freezing. Then, in February 2012, a group of snowmobilers spotted what looked like the roof of a car protruding from a snowdrift. Digging through nearly a metre of snow, they made an astonishing discovery: inside sat the missing driver, alive but severely weakened after spending almost two months trapped inside the snow-covered vehicle with little or no food. His extraordinary survival stunned doctors and scientists alike, raising questions about how the human body can endure prolonged starvation and extreme cold under exceptional circumstances. The case remains one of the most remarkable survival stories on record, highlighting the body's extraordinary ability to adapt under rare conditions while continuing to inform medical understanding of hypothermia, starvation and human resilience.Peter Skyllberg, a 44-year-old Swedish man, had apparently become stranded on a remote road after his vehicle was immobilised by heavy snowfall during late December.As reported by the BBC, over the following weeks, repeated snowstorms gradually buried the car beneath roughly one metre of snow, leaving only a small portion visible above the surface. On 17 February 2012, passing snowmobilers noticed the unusual shape beneath the snow and stopped to investigate. After digging into the drift, they found the driver sitting inside the vehicle, barely able to move or speak but still conscious. Emergency responders transported him by helicopter to hospital, where doctors began treating him for severe dehydration, malnutrition and hypothermia.Medical specialists estimated that the man had survived for close to two months with virtually no food. According to doctors treating him, he is believed to have survived primarily by melting and drinking snow, preventing fatal dehydration while his body relied on stored fat reserves for energy. Physicians also suggested that prolonged exposure to cold may have pushed his body into an extreme energy-conservation state, dramatically slowing metabolism and reducing calorie requirements.Rather than freezing, the man may have benefited from the very snow that trapped him. The thick blanket of snow covering the vehicle acted as a natural insulating layer, shielding the interior from the harshest outdoor temperatures and helping maintain a more stable environment than the open air outside.Although humans can survive for weeks without food under certain conditions, surviving for nearly two months in such an isolated environment is exceptionally rare.Doctors involved in the case described the survival as extraordinary, noting that each situation depends on numerous factors, including hydration, body fat, physical activity, environmental conditions and underlying health.The Swedish case also highlighted the protective role snow can sometimes play. While heavy snowfall often creates life-threatening situations, deep snow can also trap pockets of relatively warmer air, reducing heat loss in much the same way that insulated shelters or snow caves protect mountaineers during winter storms.The man's identity was never widely publicised, and after receiving medical treatment he gradually recovered from the ordeal.His case remains one of the most extraordinary documented examples of human endurance in modern times. Rather than surviving through extraordinary supplies or specialised equipment, he endured weeks of isolation using little more than melted snow while remaining inside a vehicle buried beneath winter drifts.The incident continues to fascinate survival experts and physicians because it demonstrates how, under exceptional circumstances, the human body can adapt far beyond what most people would consider possible. It also serves as a reminder of both the dangers of remote winter travel and the remarkable resilience that can emerge when survival depends on conserving every possible ounce of energy.
Article Summary: Peter Skyllberg, a 44-year-old Swedish man, had apparently become stranded on a remote road after his vehicle was immobilised by heavy snowfall. Snowmobilers uncovered the buried car after noticing something unusual beneath the snow. Doctors believed melted snow and an extremely slow metabolism helped keep him alive. The case challenged assumptions about the limits of human survival.
